labels.label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner is to take Holmes and Watson to the rooms
That afternoon: Miss Stoner takes Holmes and Watson to the building

note: Asked for at ¶131; by ¶132 they are at the building.
Helen's answer at ¶147 ("I never heard of her using it") takes it that the bell-rope was already there in Julia's lifetime.

label: Long ago: the original building of the house
quote: the original building of the house
note: Watson supposes that the oak may date from then.

label: Before the visit: scaffolding is put up against the end wall
quote: Some scaffolding had been erected against the end wall
note: The text does not say when; the stone-work broken into is the piercing told at ¶67.

label: A couple of years ago: the bell-rope is put in beside the bed
quote: it was only put there a couple of years ago
note: Helen's answer at ¶147 implies that it was there while Julia lived.

label: In recent times: the ventilator is made

labels.label: In recent times: the ventilator is made
A couple of years ago: the ventilator is made, one of several little changes at about the time of the bell-rope

quote: That is also quite modern
note: ¶155–156: about the same time as the bell-rope; not ordered against it or against Julia's death.

label: That afternoon: Holmes and Watson at the building, with no workmen to be seen
quote: at the moment of our visit

label: That afternoon: Holmes walks up and down the lawn, examining the outsides of the windows
quote: examined with deep attention the outsides of the windows

label: That afternoon: Holmes asks which window belongs to which room
quote: belongs to the room in which you used to sleep

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner agrees, and says she now sleeps in the middle room
quote: But I am now sleeping in the middle one

label: That afternoon: Holmes remarks that the end wall seems in no pressing need of repairs
quote: there does not seem to be any very pressing need for repairs

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner says she believes the repairs were an excuse to move her
quote: I believe that it was an excuse to move me from my room

label: That afternoon: Holmes asks about windows in the corridor
quote: There are windows in it, of course?

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner says the corridor windows are too narrow to pass through
quote: Too narrow for anyone to pass through

label: That afternoon: Holmes concludes the rooms were unapproachable from the corridor and asks Miss Stoner to bar her shutters
quote: would you have the kindness to go into your room and bar your shutters?

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner goes into her room
quote: Miss Stoner did so
note: The text does not say when she rejoins them; she is answering Holmes in the second room by ¶143.

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner bars the shutters
quote: Miss Stoner did so

label: That afternoon: Holmes makes a careful examination through the open window
quote: after a careful examination through the open window

label: That afternoon: Holmes tries in every way to force the shutter open, without success
quote: endeavoured in every way to force the shutter open

label: That afternoon: Holmes tests the hinges with his lens
quote: with his lens he tested the hinges

label: That afternoon: Holmes admits that his theory presents difficulties, and turns to the inside
quote: my theory certainly presents some difficulties

label: That afternoon: they go by a small side door into the corridor
quote: A small side door led into the whitewashed corridor

label: That afternoon: Holmes refuses to examine the third chamber
quote: Holmes refused to examine the third chamber

label: That afternoon: they pass into the second room, where the sister met her fate
quote: we passed at once to the second

label: That afternoon: Holmes draws a chair into a corner and sits silent, taking in the room
quote: Holmes drew one of the chairs into a corner and sat silent

label: That afternoon: Holmes asks where the bell communicates with
quote: Where does that bell communicate with?

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner says it goes to the housekeeper's room
quote: It goes to the housekeeper’s room

label: That afternoon: Holmes remarks that the bell-rope looks newer than the other things
quote: It looks newer than the other things?

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner says the bell-rope was put there only a couple of years ago
quote: it was only put there a couple of years ago

label: That afternoon: Holmes supposes that her sister asked for it
quote: Your sister asked for it, I suppose?

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner says she never heard of her sister using it
quote: I never heard of her using it

label: That afternoon: Holmes remarks that so nice a bell-pull seems unnecessary, and excuses himself to examine the floor
quote: it seemed unnecessary to put so nice a bell-pull there

label: That afternoon: Holmes crawls over the floor with his lens, examining the cracks between the boards
quote: crawled swiftly backward and forward

label: That afternoon: Holmes examines the wood-work panelling in the same way
quote: he did the same with the wood-work

label: That afternoon: Holmes walks over to the bed and studies it and the wall
quote: he walked over to the bed

label: That afternoon: Holmes gives the bell-rope a brisk tug
quote: gave it a brisk tug

label: That afternoon: Holmes declares the bell-rope a dummy
quote: Why, it’s a dummy

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner asks whether it won't ring
quote: Won’t it ring?

label: That afternoon: Holmes shows that the rope is fastened to a hook above the ventilator
quote: it is fastened to a hook just above where the little opening for the ventilator is

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner says she never noticed that before
quote: I never noticed that before

label: That afternoon: Holmes pulls at the rope and remarks on a ventilator opened into another room
quote: to open a ventilator into another room

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner says the ventilator is also quite modern
quote: That is also quite modern

label: That afternoon: Holmes asks whether it was done about the same time as the bell-rope
quote: Done about the same time as the bell-rope?

label: That afternoon: Miss Stoner says several little changes were carried out about that time
quote: there were several little changes carried out about that time

label: That afternoon: Holmes remarks on the dummy bell-rope and the ventilator, and proposes to go on to the inner apartment
quote: dummy bell-ropes, and ventilators which do not ventilate

label: That afternoon: they are to carry their researches into the inner apartment
quote: we shall now carry our researches into the inner apartment
note: Proposed; it has not happened by the end of this scene.
